categories.title: The 2xc − d metric (personal construction)
categories.intro: Joshua's own invented algebra. These chats are built around his rule 2xc − d = 1, which he calls a "metric for all computing", and related shorthand. It is a personal, speculative construction, not established mathematics or physics. The pages show how the chats rearranged and applied it.

entries.summary: Solving x² − x/v = mc with the quadratic formula, then a look at what changes if c is the speed of light (including a units check).
Reading handwritten notes on the definition u = logₙ v ⇔ nᵘ = v, with examples like log₆₀ 60 = 1.

entries.statusNote: Personal notation. Turn 1 is ordinary base 3 with renamed digits; the later u/p/i mapping is Joshua's own construction, not a standard numeral system.
entries.summary: A three-letter 'binary-like' system with digits u, p, i: first as base 3, then a custom mapping, plus a binary converter.
Distance = (3/2)πr: the arc length of a 270° path.
Sampling the parametric unit circle x = cos θ, y = sin θ at a 0.1 rad step, in Python.
The 3×3 identity matrix and its properties: IA = AI = A, det I = 1, I⁻¹ = I, eigenvalues all 1.
How vectors and (homogeneous) transform matrices drive sprites in real-time graphics. Qualitative, no equations.

entries.statusNote: Invented framework. 'Fold Calculus' was made up in this chat as a new formal system. It is a personal, speculative construction, not established mathematics, and has not been peer reviewed.
entries.summary: An invented 'Fold Calculus' built on sequences of crests and troughs: fold derivative, fold integral, a fundamental theorem, a worked example, and a coding loop.
Reading 100/9.65² as the variance of a sample mean (σ²/n), standard error, CEP, and a Python Monte Carlo check.
Drift rate across fields: the μ in dY = μ dt + σ dW, biased random walks, drift-diffusion models, and electron drift velocity.
Can a classical computer be modeled from a Bell state? Bell states, no-signaling, and a CHSH calculation reaching |S| = 2√2.

entries.statusNote: Exploratory. The starting expression H = xz² − x/m is Joshua's own. The chat offers possible interpretations and a simulation of one of them, not an established model.
entries.summary: Interpreting H = xz² − x/m as a qubit or anharmonic-oscillator Hamiltonian, a QuTiP simulation, and printing circuits in a terminal.

entries.statusNote: Exploratory. The relation π² = E·m − c is Joshua's own proposal. As the chat points out, it is dimensionally inconsistent as written, so it is not a physical law.
entries.summary: A units check of the proposed π² = E·m − c, and dimensionally consistent rearrangements involving E = mc².
Turning a physics notebook page into a SymPy program: v = 2πr/T, vector magnitude, and KE/PE/momentum placeholders.
Using a free-spinning bearing as a motion sensor: s = 2πrN, friction decay Iω̇ = −τ_f, and a predict-then-correct residual.
A bisection root finder in C: sign-change check, interval halving, stopping rules, and status codes.

entries.statusNote: Personal construction. The rule 2xc − d = 1 and its uses are Joshua's own invention, not established mathematics. The dollar figures come from an ad-hoc program built in the chat. They are not real valuations.
entries.summary: The chat that sets up the metric: 2xc − d = 1 is declared the "metric for all computing" and solved for d, x and c, then wrapped as a sandbox program template and a speech-to-text "valuation engine".

entries.statusNote: Personal construction. "DM" here is a symbol in Joshua's own metric notation. As the chat itself says, this is a rearrangement of his variables, not a statement about real dark matter or cosmology.
entries.summary: Rearranging DM = xc/d = b + c/d into closed forms for b, x and d, then substituting the invariant d = 2xc − 1.

entries.statusNote: Personal construction. The input string uses Joshua's own metric shorthand. The chat tries several readings of it. None of this is established mathematics.
entries.summary: Several ways to parse X=b-1c/dxcd=1/2c-1 as algebra, and the slice where two readings agree: c = 1/4, d = 4/x, X = b − x/16.

entries.statusNote: Personal construction. The fragment and the metric it is checked against are Joshua's own notation. The chat had to guess at operators like * and the prime.
entries.summary: Reading the fragment Fmc' 1d = f, *c = d − 1, c = f as a small system alongside 2xc − d = 1, and when the two expressions for d can agree.

entries.statusNote: Personal construction. The metric, the halved-Fibonacci weighting and the "analogue USD reading" are Joshua's own constructions, applied through an ad-hoc program in the chat. They are not established methods. The matcher demo uses fictional profiles only.
entries.summary: Applying 2xc − d = 1 to a piece of text, then a Fibonacci sequence with every term halved (0.5, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.5, …) and a one-way "diode" gate in a demo matcher that uses only fictional profiles.

entries.statusNote: Personal construction. This is a concept for a program, not mathematics. It sits in this group because it belongs to the same series of sandbox experiments. The capture is kept as-is.
entries.summary: The "1/10 int" idea: a ten-register integer machine with ten integer ops, plus slots reserved in memory for boot files. Almost no formulas. Captured as-is.
